extracted.intended_audience: comedy festival attendees, audience members, and performers/organizers
extracted.subtask_description: Promotional performer blurbs describing past sketch/improv/music-comedy acts — summarizing style, tone, format, training, credits, and influences for festival audiences and programmers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uncomfortable, uncompromising, unexpected / boundary-crossing
rubrics_metrics.description: Uncomfortable, uncompromising, unexpected; ... breaks boundaries, crosses the line and confronts social norms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From 15 Minutes Away: positions the act as boundary-pushing and confrontational in subject matter and tone — implies value placed on surprise, risk-taking, and challenging norms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversity and representation in cast
rubrics_metrics.description: We’ve got a diverse cast of women, queer and POC comedians.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 15 Minutes Away explicitly highlights women, queer, and POC representation as a feature — suggests casting diversity is a stated criterion/feature for some acts.

rubrics_metrics.name: UCB/Second City/Magnet-style training and house-team lineage
rubrics_metrics.description: We’re a New York City based team doing UCB style sketch comedy; cast trained by Second City, the Upright Citizen's Brigade, Washington Improv Theater, the District Improv, and Dojo Comedy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple bios reference specific schools/house teams (UCB, Second City, Magnet, The PIT). Presence of formal/improv training or house-team affiliation is presented as a signifier of style and quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional industry credits and commercial success
rubrics_metrics.description: Actors and writers featured on Netflix, HBO, Comedy Central... sold commercial ideas and content to brands such as Doritos, Legos, and Anheuser-Busch InBev.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bios repeatedly list TV credits, commercial work, and brand deals as credentials: used as evidence of legitimacy and success (e.g., cast on 'What We Do In The Shadows', writing for The Daily Show).

rubrics_metrics.name: Festival recognition and awards
rubrics_metrics.description: Winners of Judges Choice award DC Sketchfest's 24-hour sketch contest; Best in Fest at the Columbus Brew HaHa and Atlanta Sketchfest; Best Ensemble; 'Best of the Fest' awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Festival selections, awards, and headliner spots are cited as markers of accomplishment and likely selection criteria for quality and reputation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone: dark, cerebral, and absurd
rubrics_metrics.description: Specializing in the dark, the cerebral, and the absurd.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acts (e.g., Bad Medicine) are described by tone; 'dark, cerebral, absurd' signals an aesthetic preference or category for audiences and programmers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Loose, improvised feel vs scripted writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Shows have a loose, improvised feel that will leave you saying 'that was so dumb, I loved it'. / Mostly improvisors, NEVER improvised. MIST is a group of improv enthusiasts who decided to stop winging it and start writing it down!
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes spectrum from improvisational-feel performances to scripted sketch born from improv; methods (improv-to-sketch, script-to-stage) are presented as distinguishing production approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: High-concept, surreal, deranged characters and musical parodies
rubrics_metrics.description: Deranged characters, musical parodies, and surreal scenarios collide in the most unexpected ways.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some groups emphasize surrealism, high-concept premises, and musical parody as core features of their work — signaling format and comedic approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vaudeville, physical comedy, and clowning
rubrics_metrics.description: Refreshingly original and delightfully vaudevillian. / A mix of absurdism, clowning, physical comedy, and dark humor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vaudeville and physical performance elements (clowning, physicality) are identified as deliberate stylistic choices for some acts (e.g., Brandy Alexander, Grace and the Gang).

rubrics_metrics.name: Solo performer / one-person shows
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Danielle She/Her' is a one-woman sketch show about and by Danielle Steger. / solo character shows and one-man/one-woman formats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Single-performer formats and solo character shows are noted as a distinct mode with its own honors and festival presence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fanfiction, parody and mash-up formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Lose yourself in wild flights of fancy about your favorite fictional characters!... Be prepared for: crossovers, self-inserts, wild pairings, Mary Sue and Gary Stus, love triangles, love squares, plus tropes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fanfiction-based parody/storytelling is presented as a specialized sketch format relying on audience familiarity with franchises and tropes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensemble focus and community-building / teaching
rubrics_metrics.description: A focus on the power of ensemble comedy... regularly host workshops throughout the year... dedicated to fostering local talent and building comedy around community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Groups like Rails Comedy emphasize ensemble cohesion and community engagement (workshops, local talent development) as part of their mission and value to the scene.

rubrics_metrics.name: Loud, chaotic absurdism and high-energy engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Specializes in a signature—some might even say jarring—brand of loud, chaotic absurdism. There will be comedians yelling at each other, themselves, and you, the audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High-energy, intentionally chaotic performance styles (yelling, chaotic staging) are described as a deliberate approach to audience engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of music and original songs / musical comedy
rubrics_metrics.description: There will be a ukulele player, bookending each sketch with original songs and amusing covers. / musical numbers, celebrity impressions, and more!
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Musical elements (ukulele, songs, musical parody) are recurring production features and an explicit draw for some acts (e.g., High Dramma, Time to Kill).

rubrics_metrics.name: Satire, topicality, and appearances on satire/news outlets
rubrics_metrics.description: Writing has appeared on satire and humor websites like McSweeney’s, Hard Drive, and The Onion. / writers and producers at The Daily Show, The Tonight Show...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Links to topical satire, news-parody outlets, and late-night writing credits indicate a style grounded in topical satire and cultural commentary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Queer themes and LGBTQIA+ focus
rubrics_metrics.description: Big characters, queer themes... The nation’s premier LGBTQIA+ sketch team makes their DC debut!
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acts explicitly foreground queer content and identity as part of their comedic voice and target audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strong character work and big characters
rubrics_metrics.description: Bring big characters, queer themes, and lots of shouting. / deranged characters...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasis on memorable, exaggerated characters as a primary comedic engine — frequently highlighted in bios as what to expect on stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-platform viral/video content and multimedia
rubrics_metrics.description: sketches, songs, and viral videos. / absurd video sketches are known for sweeping audiences into a phantasmagoric swirl...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some teams highlight video and viral content alongside live performance as part of their creative footprint and measures of reach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Friendly/inclusive tone versus explicit/mature content
rubrics_metrics.description: They promise to deliver laughs for the whole family! / reviewers said 'I have never laughed so fucking hard' (explicit adult language)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bios indicate a spectrum from family-friendly comedy to explicit adult humor; audience suitability is a communicated feature of the act.
